financials_interim.notes: First financial_statements entry for this symbol. Single set of statements, no Group/Company split. IMPORTANT EXTRACTION CAVEAT: this PDF's text layer has a genuine column-order bug in several subtotal rows (non-current assets, non-current liabilities, current liabilities, and the income statement's profit lines from Operating Profit downward) -- the two column headers '30th June 2026' / '31st March 2026' (balance sheet) and '2026-27' / '2025-26' (income statement) get transposed relative to the individual line items in parts of the raw extraction. Every figure entered here was cross-verified two ways before use: (1) balance sheet identity (non-current + current assets = total assets; total equity + total liabilities = total assets), and (2) EPS = PAT / 532,465,705 shares in issue (note 10), which pins down which profit figures belong to which quarter unambiguously (2.87 for this quarter, 4.36 for the June-2025 comparative). Cash flow is NOT entered here because the same column-order ambiguity affects it and could not be independently cross-checked with the same confidence (the balance-sheet cash movement, Rs.2,200,219k, doesn't cleanly resolve which cash flow column is which without further assumptions) -- rather than risk wrong figures, cash_from_operations/capex/cash_from_investing/cash_from_financing are left blank. long_term_borrowings entered as 0: no non-current interest-bearing borrowings line exists on this balance sheet (only current 'Interest Bearing Borrowings'). total_liabilities = non-current liabilities (537,733) + current liabilities (34,055,305) = 34,593,038, which reconciles exactly with total assets (128,161,636) minus total equity (93,568,598).

interim_updates.note_text: Lanka IOC posted Rs.92.11bn revenue for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 47% YoY, but profit moved sharply the other way: gross margin nearly halved (7.67% to 4.11%), operating profit fell 41% (Rs.1.87bn to Rs.1.09bn), and PAT fell 34% (Rs.2.32bn to Rs.1.53bn) despite the strong top-line growth. This is a margin-compression story, not a demand or volume problem -- revenue grew faster than cost of sales did not, i.e. cost of sales grew even faster than revenue (up roughly 53% vs revenue's 47%), consistent with an oil marketing company facing higher import costs (crude/refined product prices, or Rupee depreciation raising the cost of imports) that regulated retail pricing did not fully pass through within the quarter. This filing contains no chairperson's commentary explaining the mechanism, so the specific driver (global oil prices vs FX vs regulatory pricing lag) is inferred context, not a stated fact in the document itself.
interim_updates.gaps_note: This PDF's text extraction has a column-order bug in several subtotal rows -- every figure entered here was independently cross-verified via the balance-sheet accounting identity and via EPS = PAT / 532,465,705 shares in issue before being used, to make sure the correct quarter's figures were not swapped with the comparative quarter's. Cash flow figures were NOT entered because the same ambiguity affects that statement and could not be resolved with the same confidence -- better to omit than risk an incorrect figure. No QoQ comparison is possible: no other interim quarter close to this one (e.g. 31 March 2026) has been collected for LIOC, only this filing and an older one for the period ended 30 September 2025.
interim_updates.takeaway: A textbook regulated-fuel-retailer squeeze: strong revenue growth from higher prices/volumes, but gross margin nearly halved, wiping out most of the topline gain by the operating-profit line. Worth watching whether margin recovers in the next quarter (suggesting a timing lag in price pass-through) or persists (suggesting a structural cost increase).
operational_highlights: Revenue Rs.92.11bn, up 47% YoY, but gross margin nearly halved (7.67% to 4.11%)
Operating profit Rs.1.09bn, down 41% YoY (Rs.1.87bn a year earlier); PAT Rs.1.53bn, down 34% YoY (Rs.2.32bn a year earlier)
EPS Rs.2.87, down from Rs.4.36 a year earlier
This is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol -- no prior interim data was on file before this one
key_drivers: The entire YoY profit decline is a gross-margin story: revenue grew 47% but gross profit fell 21%, meaning cost of sales grew roughly 53% -- faster than revenue -- squeezing margin from 7.67% to 4.11%

Plausible causes for an oil marketing company (not confirmed by this filing, which has no MD&A section): higher global crude/refined-product import costs, Rupee depreciation raising the cost of imports (the Rupee depreciated materially during this same quarter per other CSE-listed companies' Q1 FY2026/27 filings), or a lag between import cost increases and regulated retail price adjustments

Finance income grew faster than finance expenses fell (both roughly proportionate to a larger cash/investment base and new interest-bearing borrowings taken on during the quarter, per the balance sheet), providing a modest partial offset below the operating-profit line
